column1: A **profile** is one game in your library. GameTimeNext records the playtime of every session, keeps track of your playthroughs and can launch the game directly.
> When a game of a profile is running, GameTimeNext detects it automatically and switches to its profile. You don't have to start monitoring by hand.

column3: Filters the list by profile name.

column1: Select a profile to see its details on the right:
- **Activity**: total playtime, today, last session, first and last played
- **Current playthrough**: progress of the running playthrough
- **Launch game** starts the game, **Start monitoring** records the playtime manually (e.g. for console games)
- *Current playthrough completed* / *Cancel current playthrough* (while one is running)
- **Archive profile** / **Unarchive profile**: archived profiles are hidden from the library
- **Steam** → *Show steam library* (only for profiles linked with Steam)
Checked entries are shown, uncheck what you want to hide.

column3: Unplayed, In Progress, Paused, Completed, Cancelled
*Playable* (the game's .exe is found in its folder), *Not playable*

column1: Options: **Recently played only** (last 14 days) and **Show archived**. **Reset** shows the whole library again.
- **Platform**: use the 🧙 wizard to add a new one
- **Game folder**: folder that contains the game's `.exe`. Required to detect and launch the game.
- **Target play style** and estimated times: **Enter manual** opens a dialog with a link to *HowLongToBeat*
Set the cover either with **Browse local…** or with **SteamGridDB…**, then crop it.
- **Steam import** takes over name, folder and data of a Steam game
- **Remove link** unlinks the profile from Steam
- **Change accent colors based on this profile**: the app takes on the colors of the cover while the profile is active
- **Enable HDR on game start**, **blackout side monitors** (optionally overriding the global setting)
Free tags to group and filter your library.
> Starting a game without an active playthrough asks whether a new one should be created. Playtime is always recorded in a playthrough.
